chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir, from ʿUmar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the iqamah without adhan in the Maghrib prayer, and he said: There is no harm in it, but I do not like that you make a habit of that.

So this does not contradict what we have presented earlier, because it is only permissible for him to suffice with the iqamah in these prayers when there is some incidental circumstance or impediment. His statement, 'I do not like that you make a habit of that,' indicates that what is preferable is to perform it.

key_terms.الْأَوْلَى: That which is preferable or more appropriate.
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: The call immediately preceding the commencement of salat (prayer).
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: The Maghrib salat (prayer), performed after sunset.
key_terms.تَعْتَادَ: To make something a habitual or regular practice.
key_terms.عَارِضٍ: A temporary circumstance or incidental excuse.
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: An expression indicating permissibility and absence of harm.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite the iqamah without the adhan for Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that giving only the iqamah for Maghrib prayer, without the adhan, is permissible and not inherently problematic. However, the Imam عليه السلام discourages making this a regular practice, showing that the preferred sunnah (prophetic tradition) is to perform both the adhan and the iqamah except in cases of excuse or hindrance.
